tagline: Across the slate belt and the stumps of old volcanoes.
intro: From Asheboro, NC 49 runs southwest across the Carolina Slate Belt, where buildings and fences were once built of slate, skirts the northern foothills of the Uwharrie Mountains, then crosses the Yadkin on its way to Mount Pleasant and Concord. The main route is 50.7 miles. An extension on NC 109 through Denton adds 22.4.

The Uwharries are what is left of a chain of volcanoes active some 550 million years ago, worn down to isolated, heavily eroded hills. They were once cleared for timber and farms. They became a national forest in 1961, and the woods have come back. Corn and winter wheat grow along the road.

moments.title: Denton
moments.text: Once Finch's Cross Roads, the town borrowed its name from Texas in 1878 and later shipped nearly 200,000 railroad cross ties a year at its peak.

moments.title: Tuckertown crossing
moments.text: NC 49 crosses the Yadkin on the bridge at Tuckertown, where the reservoir fills a narrow valley at the western edge of the Uwharries.

moments.title: Reed Gold Mine
moments.text: About eight miles south of Mount Pleasant, a boy found a 17-pound yellow rock in Little Meadow Creek in 1799, and the family used it as a doorstop for three years.
